passage:
The school cafeteria changed its menu. Instead of selling only fried food and sweet drinks, it added vegetable soup, fruit boxes, and rice balls.
Many students were unhappy at first. They said healthy food was boring. The cafeteria workers listened and changed the recipes. They added more colors, better sauces, and a "student choice" meal every Friday.
After a month, the fruit boxes sold out almost every day. The vegetable soup became popular in winter.
The cafeteria did not force students to love healthy food. It made healthy food easier to choose.
The principal said this was the real goal. Good choices should not feel like punishment. They should feel possible.
